title: Coexistence of positive metric entropy and elliptic islands for analytic symplectomorphisms of closed analytic symplectic surfaces
source_title: Coexistence of chaotic and elliptic behaviors among analytic, symplectic diffeomorphisms of any surface
author: Pierre Berger
difficulty_reason: Analytic bump functions are unavailable, so the desired coexistence cannot be produced by ordinary local smooth pasting. The source constructs an analytic symplectic blow-up, compatible involution quotient and Hamiltonian cap, then blows down the cap boundary while preserving the stochastic piece. It proves the collar gluing and performs the sphere/torus/pants constructions for all genera, remaining substantive surgery obligations after the stated normal-form foundations are allowed.

proof_review.note: Full article retained as conservative closed context for notation, global assumptions, diagrams and references. Exact primary and supporting physical proof pages are recorded separately. TheoremA on closed analytic symplectic surfaces, existence only; no perturbative density or every-isotopy-class conjecture claimed. Read exact statement2–3 and every new surgery/cap/gluing construction7–19; proof20 retains the cited analytic symplectic form normalization [DM90]. Linear torus Anosov and angle-action/Moser normal forms are prior foundations. Claim3.1 literal exponent display tends to infinity, while its explicit linear Anosov construction and later20 correctly use a finite positive constant; selected theorem only requires positive entropy. Claim3.2 describes both critical Hessians as positive whereas its explicit blow-downs occur on level circles of signs plus/minus epsilon squared; only definite/elliptic property used by TheoremA is selected. Preserve these literal support descriptions and the fully written Hamiltonian cap, no new quantitative dynamics proof supplied. No generalized-cap/pseudo-Anosov or isotopy variants counted.
